smells.finding: episode_capture.py:158-179 and :196-220 both carry the same four-step sequence: `import context_manifest as cm`, compose the destination via `cm.manifest_path(manifest_root(base_dir), checklist.get('work_id'), <step>)`, `if destination.exists(): return destination`, `cm.write_manifest(..., destination)`. The two copies already DISAGREE on the third argument -- the success path names the file after `manifest['step']` (i.e. `active_id(cl)`), the stub path after `iid`. On any run where the two differ (the implementer's own out-of-scope observation 2: an earlier blocked gate), the manifest and its failure stub target different files, and the write-if-absent guard in each copy cannot see the other's file. Extracting a single `_place(checklist, base_dir, step) -> Path` used by both would make the divergence a deliberate one-line argument rather than a latent drift between two copies. Observation, not a blocker: the divergent case is unreachable through normal gated flow.
`emit_step_manifest` and `_write_failure_stub` are almost entirely calls into `context_manifest` (`build_manifest`, `manifest_path`, `write_manifest`) and hold no state of their own.

override.repo_standard: skills/_shared/global-everyone.md, 'Deep-module vocabulary': Seam -- where an interface lives, its placement is its own decision; Adapter -- a thing satisfying an interface at a seam. Plus PLAN_CRITIC_DISPOSITION.md D1, which adopts start()/reopen() as the seam.
override.reason: Envy of the producer is this module's entire job description. It is the adapter between the engine's status machine and a deliberately when/where-agnostic producer, and its own docstring scopes it to exactly the three decisions the producer refuses to make (when, which roots, where). Moving the logic into `context_manifest` would re-import scheduling into a module #300 froze as opinion-free; moving it into the engine is what D1 and the handoff explicitly forbid.

override.repo_standard: skills/_shared/global-crew.md, Implementation discipline: 'Match the surrounding code's naming, labeling, and in-file documentation conventions' and 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction.'

Introducing a parameter object would make the seam's signature diverge from every neighbouring verb it is called beside, and would be exactly the speculative abstraction the discipline forbids for a two-call-site clump.

override.repo_standard: context_manifest.ROOT_TOKENS is the frozen #300 contract surface (docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md documents `context_refs.root` as one of skill|repo|durable, a JSON-authored string); PLAN_CRITIC_DISPOSITION.md D2 requires the frozen contract be 'satisfied as written rather than reinterpreted'.
override.reason: The tokens originate as JSON strings in authored checklists and are validated once, upstream, by `context_manifest.resolve`. A local enum would have to be converted back to those strings at the only boundary that matters and would give this module a second, competing vocabulary for a contract it does not own. `resolve_roots` is keyed in `ROOT_TOKENS` order precisely to stay subordinate to that contract.

smells.finding: Making one manifest appear requires coordinated edits in four places, and the change only landed three of them. scripts/checklist_engine.py (import shim + two call sites + reopen's base_dir + _run_verb threading), scripts/episode_capture.py, tests/ -- and scripts/install_constellation.py SKILL_SCRIPT_BUNDLES, which was NOT touched. Because the fourth site was missed, the feature is inert in every installed skill (see r1/r4). That is the diagnostic value of this smell here: the change's true blast radius spans a packaging table that lives in a different file and has no mechanical link to the engine's imports, so nothing made the omission visible. The remedy is the same either way -- bundle episode_capture.py, context_manifest.py and agent_work_root.py with every engine-carrying skill and add a test asserting the bundle -- which also collapses the surgery to a single declared dependency set.

`repo_root`, `resolve_roots` and `manifest_root` are public, individually typed, and each has exactly one production caller (`emit_step_manifest`); `episode_capture.py` also carries an `if __name__ == '__main__'` block whose only purpose is to print resolved roots.

override.repo_standard: skills/_shared/global-everyone.md, 'Deep-module vocabulary': 'The interface is the test surface. Test through it, not past it; wanting to reach behind it means the module is the wrong shape.'
override.reason: These are not anticipated future callers -- they are the test surface the close criteria require. Criterion 3 demands the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE PATH be asserted, not the code that produced it; the seven RootResolution tests can only do that because `resolve_roots` and `repo_root` are reachable independently of an engine run, and my own independent mutants MUT-A/MUT-B were only killable through them. The `__main__` block is documented as a diagnostic, not an interface, and deliberately ships no CLI verb -- the same restraint context_manifest.py exercises.

The neighbouring modules context_manifest.py, checklist_engine.py and agent_work_root.py all carry the same rationale-dense docstring convention.
override.reason: Deodorant masks unclear code; here the prose carries decisions the code physically cannot express and that a reader would otherwise have to re-derive or get wrong. The clearest instance is episode_capture.py:54-57 -- the comment naming `durable_agent_work()` as the WRONG neighbouring helper -- which documents the exact double-nesting trap close criterion 3 is built around, a trap that produces a structurally valid manifest and a green suite when got wrong. Deleting the prose would not simplify one line of logic; it would delete the only record of why `durable_root(repo)` and not `durable_root(base_dir)`. It is also not compensating for bad names: every identifier here reads plainly on its own.
